metadata.title: Piotr J. Borowiecki · Full-Stack Software Engineer
metadata.description: Full-stack software engineer at IBM, building payment software for banks. TypeScript, React and TanStack, open source, and AI-assisted engineering done properly.

hero.name: Piotr J. Borowiecki
hero.role: I build software where small mistakes are expensive.
hero.building: At IBM, I work on payment software used by banks. On my own, I design and ship complete products, with a focus on performance, accessibility and code that stays maintainable.
hero.portraitAlt: Portrait of Piotr J. Borowiecki in a navy blazer and white shirt, arms folded, looking at the camera
hero.focusPaymentsDesc: Message entry and repair for IBM Financial Transaction Manager, where every field has to be exactly right.
hero.focusProductsDesc: From the data model to production: storefronts, booking systems and an open-source SaaS foundation.
hero.focusAiDesc: AI agents in daily work, inside a harness of tests, guardrails and review, so speed never costs quality.

about.backgroundText: A BSc in Computer Science from Durham University (UK), with a dissertation on probabilistic time-series forecasting with diffusion models. Then full-time freelance product work and, since 2024, enterprise engineering at IBM.
about.expertiseText: I work across the stack and across languages: TypeScript and React at the core, with Go, Python and Java where they fit. I choose technology for what it does for the product, which usually means fewer moving parts and code that’s easy to change.
about.photoAlt: Piotr J. Borowiecki seated at a boardroom table beside floor-to-ceiling windows, a closed laptop and notebook in front of him
about.title: Where precision isn’t optional.
about.description: At IBM, I work on Financial Transaction Manager, a payments platform for financial institutions, where reliability and precision are non-negotiable. It’s the standard I hold all my work to.
about.quote: Reliability isn’t a property of the software. It’s how the work gets done.
about.ownershipBody: From the data model to the last edge case in the interface, and after it ships.
about.qualityBody: Accessibility, performance and tests from the first commit, not as a pass at the end.
about.candourBody: If something won’t work, the team hears it from me first, with an alternative attached.

philosophy.photoAlt: Piotr J. Borowiecki holding a marker beside a whiteboard covered in a hand-drawn system diagram
philosophy.label: Approach
philosophy.title: Complexity is expensive. Clarity compounds.
philosophy.messTitle: Long-lived systems tend to drift here.
philosophy.messBody: Systems nobody dares to touch. Integrations held together by habit. AI bolted on wherever it would fit. Every release slower and riskier than the last, and no one able to say exactly why.
philosophy.clearBody: One architecture, with clear boundaries and clear ownership, and nothing in it that hasn’t earned its place. The team moves faster, changes become predictable, and every next decision gets easier instead of harder.
philosophy.signoff: Getting from the first picture to the second is the work I enjoy most.
philosophy.diagramTitle: An architecture diagram that starts as a tangle of direct calls into one shared database, with seven open findings, and resolves into clean layers: clients, edge, domains that each own their data, an event bus, downstream consumers and a shared platform, with no open findings.

ai.label: AI in practice
ai.title: Output is cheap now. Judgment isn’t.
ai.intro: I work with AI coding agents every day, within enterprise standards at IBM and in my own projects. The results depend less on the model than on what surrounds it.
ai.messTitle: Without it, you get slop at speed.
ai.messBody: Code that looks right and isn’t. Agents that drift. A codebase nobody can untangle a year from now, produced faster than anyone can review it.
ai.guardrailsBody: What AI may touch, what it may never touch, and what happens when it’s wrong. Set before the first line is written.
ai.harnessBody: Tests, evaluations and review loops that prove the output instead of trusting it. Nothing counts until it passes.
ai.judgmentBody: Telling good from merely plausible takes years of building real systems. It’s the one part you can’t prompt.
ai.diagramTitle: A bundle of tangled strands labelled AI output passes through three gates, guardrails, harness and judgment. Most strands stop at a gate, and a few clean parallel lines reach production.
ai.closing: The return is measured in what you ship and what you never have to rebuild. This site is built that way, in the open.

person.label: About
person.title: Most of my work is handling complexity.
person.story1: I studied Computer Science at Durham University in the UK, and today I work at IBM on Financial Transaction Manager, a platform financial institutions use to orchestrate and monitor their payments.
person.story2: My area is payment message entry and repair, across the interface and the backend-for-frontend. I also rebuilt the product’s core data table and moved a large part of the application onto one shared approach to time zones and formatting.
person.story3: Everyone wants software that works. I want hard problems, clear ownership and people who care about the quality under the hood as much as I do. If that sounds like your team, I’d like to hear from you.
person.portraitAlt: Piotr J. Borowiecki standing in a navy suit, one hand in his pocket, against a dark studio backdrop
person.proofTitle: You don’t have to take my word for it.
person.ibmBody: Software engineer on Financial Transaction Manager, payment software used by banks.
person.nhsBody: University project, built alongside their developers.
person.liveBody: An open-source SaaS foundation I designed and built, with {stars, number}+ stars on GitHub.
person.storyLead: I’m Piotr, a full-stack software engineer who cares about the details that decide whether software can be trusted.
person.closingLead: I’m always happy to talk about good engineering.
person.storyPassion: Technology is also my passion. Most of my own time goes into building, and most of what’s left goes into reading.
person.storyFocus: Before IBM, I freelanced full-time as the sole engineer on complete products, including a bilingual storefront for a jewellery brand and online booking for a veterinary clinic. I enjoy work with a complex domain behind it most: financial data, detailed standards and workflows where a small mistake has a price.
person.storyStack: My core stack is TypeScript, React and the TanStack libraries, Node.js and Bun, PostgreSQL or SQLite with Drizzle, running on Cloudflare Workers, with Go, Python and Java when the problem calls for them.
person.storyTeach: I’m also building <react>ReactProjects.com</react> and <angular>AngularProjects.com</angular>, course platforms where developers learn to build advanced, real-world projects from scratch, step by step.
person.teachBody: Course platforms I’m building, teaching advanced projects step by step.

marte.category: Premium e-commerce platform for a Polish jewellery brand
marte.summary: A bilingual storefront and back office for a Polish jewellery brand, with customer accounts, order management and an audit log.
marte.challenge: The brand needed a premium storefront that stayed fast, and a back office for its catalogue, orders and customers.
marte.solution: One TanStack Start application on Cloudflare Workers, with D1, KV, R2, Durable Objects and Queues, Stripe checkout and GSAP motion.
marte.outcome: A fast, bilingual storefront and a back office with order management and an audit log, with no servers to maintain.

saasyland.category: Production-ready SaaS foundation that saves teams hundreds of hours
saasyland.summary: An opinionated SaaS starter kit: one command scaffolds auth, billing, an admin and a visual page builder.
saasyland.challenge: Starting a new SaaS requires configuring authentication, databases, payment gateways, and dashboards from scratch. This repetitive boilerplate wastes valuable development time and delays time-to-market.
saasyland.solution: One command scaffolds a TanStack Start application on Cloudflare with authentication, billing, i18n and an admin console, under strict lint and a 100% coverage gate.
saasyland.outcome: An open-source foundation with 400+ stars and 100+ forks on GitHub.
